claimBoundary: On one normal Chrome/WebGPU implementation, ONNX Runtime WebGPU writes a preallocated GPUBuffer and Three.js reads that identical object through a 24-byte read-only TSL storage binding without mapping, CPU upload, or a GPU copy involving the target. The input originates on the CPU and the separate integer render target is read back only as a post-render correctness oracle; this protocol makes no performance or cross-device universality claim.

candidate.subject: WebGPU: Harden borrowed storage buffer adoption

order: Three exact oracle and visual render
explicitly release the first borrowed attribute from Three's attribute manager, then dispose geometry, materials, render target, and renderer
ORT run 2 into the same target
fresh Three renderer and attribute exact oracle
explicitly release the second borrowed attribute, then dispose the second Three resources

assertions: the candidate, outer source, Three build, ORT bundle, ORT wasm, and embedded model are content-addressed
one explicitly-created GPUDevice is passed to both ONNX Runtime WebGPU and each Three WebGPURenderer
ORT returns the supplied preallocated Tensor and its exact GPUBuffer object on both runs
an ORT target-containing bind group is set before a compute dispatch on both runs
every decisive dispatch and draw is encoded into a finished command buffer that is submitted on the target GPUDevice
target-using compute and draw commands occur only in their two declared ORT and Three proof phases

Three caches and binds the identical target with explicit offset 0, size 24, no dynamic offset, a read-only-storage layout, and matching generated WGSL whose target variable is read by both active pipeline stages before each proof draw
the 32-byte target is never mapped, CPU-written, cleared, copied, used as vertex/index/indirect data, or destroyed before owner cleanup
each Three attribute manager and backend cache contains the borrowed attribute before explicit release and neither retains it afterward
explicit borrowed-attribute release and both renderer disposals leave the target undestroyed
a distinct second ORT output and fresh Three renderer prove target reuse after teardown
both rgba32uint readbacks contain only exact expected float-bit tuples at their expected spatial locations
shader compilation messages, GPU errors, page errors, network errors, and unexpected device loss are absent
the screenshot is captured before teardown and truthfully labels the bounded claim
